new_public_evidence.source: Wang & Ramdas (2025), Anytime-valid t-tests and confidence sequences for Gaussian means with unknown variance
new_public_evidence.result: Two genuine e-process constructions exist for Gaussian mean inference with unknown variance. They are promising for the r82 mean-direction bottleneck, but their exact filtration must be checked before repeatedly combining one frozen reference with future blocks inside the common-increment delayed-start recursion.

new_public_evidence.source: Grunwald, de Heide & Koolen (2024), Safe testing
new_public_evidence.result: Safe t-test/right-Haar e-values handle nuisance scale and can be sequentially coherent, while the paper explicitly warns that optional-continuation safety depends on the filtration. This supports a t-style replacement only with a fresh conditional-e proof for the frozen-reference reuse pattern.

new_public_evidence.source: Shaer, Bar, Prinster & Romano (2026), Testing For Distribution Shifts with Conditional Conformal Test Martingales
new_public_evidence.result: Algorithm-level source text gives the finite-reference DKW-corrected betting factor and ONS update. The r81 comparison in this run used that actual conditional-CTM update rather than a heuristic drift approximation.

derived_results.claim: The r82 reference chi-square quantiles, endpoint ratios cU/cL, variance likelihood factors and mean shift floor reproduce to double precision under 100-decimal monotone bisection. CDF residuals at the chi-square bracket endpoints are around 1e-74 with opposite signs.
derived_results.scope: This is strong arbitrary-precision numerical verification, not a true machine-directed interval certificate because the transcendental evaluator itself was not interval-certified.

derived_results.claim: On an 11-direction exact Gaussian KL=1 grid, the r82 delayed-start common-increment block mixture materially outperforms the r81 start-at-monitoring conditional-CTM/p-to-e portfolio as changepoint time grows, while r81 is slightly faster for immediate changes.
derived_results.interpretation: The r81 wealth begins at monitoring time and can decay before a late change. The r82 heavy-tail delayed-start mixture preserves fresh post-change components while remaining O(1) state because all starts share the same block increment.

derived_results.claim: In 2000 common implementation null paths monitored for 100000 samples, the r82 hybrid produced 5 false alarms (0.0025) and r81 produced 9 (0.0045).
derived_results.scope: Engineering smoke only; theoretical PFA remains the analytic union/e-process result and is not inferred from this finite simulation.

derived_results.claim: Across 4400 immediate-change path-direction cases, adding the tiny-budget first-start r77 t/F sentinel made the r82 hybrid earlier than guard-only in 18 cases, later in 2 because the guard alpha was correspondingly reduced, and identical in 4380. Its retained value is therefore primarily finite-sample first-start certification over unbounded Gaussian KL>=1, not empirical speed on this grid.

A mean-block m=16 / direction weights {variance:0.20 each, mean:0.30 each} tuning improved some pre10000 empirical mean q90 values from 144 to 128 samples, but the conservative component 95% bound at prechange 1e6 worsened from 2400 raw samples for current m32/w0.25 to 2448. The current m32 equal-weight design is retained pending a stronger theorem-compatible mean factor.

negative_or_scope_evidence: The high-precision quantile check is not a substitute for a machine-certified interval implementation; do not relabel it as directed-rounding proof.
The matched simulation covers a finite exact-KL=1 Gaussian grid, not the entire KL>=1 continuum and not non-Gaussian or dependent changes.
Immediate-change speed is not uniformly improved: r81's raw conditional CTM/p-to-e route has a lower worst q90 on the tested immediate grid.
The r77 first-start sentinel adds little empirical speed once the r82 block guard is present on the tested grid, although it still supplies a stronger short-horizon analytic power certificate.
Wang-Ramdas/safe-t e-processes cannot be dropped into the frozen-reference repeated-block design without checking the exact conditional filtration and common-increment property.

candidate_new.mechanism: Retain the r82 four-direction fixed-reference block e-process with a telescoping heavy-tail delayed-start prior and exact O(1) recursion. Treat the r77 sentinel as a certification companion, not a required latency accelerator. Investigate a nuisance-aware t-style mean factor only if it remains a conditional e-value when the same frozen reference is reused and the per-block increment is common to all delayed starts.
candidate_new.status: strong engineering support within Gaussian iid KL=1 grid plus existing symbolic PFA/full-coverage certificate; machine interval layer and improved mean-factor proof remain open

frontier: Instantiate the Wang-Ramdas or safe-testing t-style Gaussian mean e-factor under the exact frozen-reference-plus-future-block filtration. Prove or refute conditional e-validity when the same reference is reused across blocks and whether the resulting increment is identical across all candidate starts.
If the t-style route fails the common-increment/conditional-validity requirement, keep the r82 confidence-bound exponential mean factor rather than sacrificing O(1) delayed-start state.

Replace the current arbitrary-precision monotone quantile brackets with a true directed-rounding/interval implementation; if no rigorous special-function enclosure is available, keep symbolic chi-square/normal quantiles as the authoritative certificate layer and explicitly mark decimals non-machine-certified.

Only after a genuinely new mean factor exists, rerun the matched common-random comparison at immediate, 1k, 10k and 100k changepoints. Do not spend more frontier on block-size/weight tuning that improves simulation while weakening the current conservative power bound.
Generalize the delayed-start common-increment compression pattern outside Gaussian families only after deriving family-specific conditional e-factors; no heavy-tail or dependence transfer is implied.
exact_next_action: Open the formula-level Wang-Ramdas canonical-filtration and safe-t constructions and test them against the exact r82 reuse filtration: frozen 684-sample reference, deterministic future blocks, arbitrary delayed starts sharing one block increment. Either derive a conditional e-factor with common increments and a tighter mean-shift growth bound, or produce a counterexample/filtration obstruction and retain r82 unchanged. In parallel seek a truly interval-certified chi-square/normal quantile implementation for the existing constants.
